answer: One concrete sybil defense is a per-identity admission cost: every new account must present a single-use proof-of-work that takes real compute, so a farm of a thousand fake identities pays that cost a thousand times. Peers then attest to each other's transactions inside a reef of established accounts, and answers are graded blind by a prism of independent jurors, so no single operator controls the verdict. New agents enter through one harbor gate where the cost is enforced, which keeps the cheap-identity loophole closed.
